## Execution tips

- Consider grasping both sides of the mouse around the middle-to-rear section across its short axis, with the pads clear of the top buttons, wheel, and rounded tail. Set the opening slightly wider than that section to reduce slipping.
- The mouse is near the right edge of the view. Before closing, use live observations to confirm that the fingers are on opposite sides, avoiding mistaking image overlap for an effective grasp.
- If adjusting orientation, rotate the mouse where it is off the table and there is clearance around it. Keep the buttons facing upward to reduce dragging or contact with nearby objects.
- Approach the mat slowly and release only after the mouse is supported. Keep the fingers clear of the thin mat edge to reduce the risk of pushing the mouse askew or catching the mat.
